logo.requirement: Use the genuine ITCS logo. Preserve its proportions.
logo.fallback_rule: If the asset is missing, retrieve an authorised official asset or request it. Do not invent a replacement logo.

typography.primary: Reuse the existing project's ITCS sans-serif font if available. Otherwise choose a clean geometric sans-serif with clear letterforms.
typography.display: Medium or regular weight, tight but readable tracking, restrained line height.
typography.body: Readable sans-serif with comfortable line spacing.
guidance: Do not make supporting text excessively tiny.
Use at least 16px for mobile form inputs.
Use monospaced text selectively for receipt metadata and printer status.
Maintain a clear hierarchy between headings, explanations and actions.

layout.principle: Align sections consistently. Avoid narrow floating content blocks that feel disconnected from the page.

avoid: Overly distressed textures that reduce readability

printer.headline: Business IT. All connected.
printer.eyebrow: Managed IT support · Cyber security · Telecoms

printer.instruction: Choose either side. Get the essentials.

composition.desktop: Wide central red printer with three service choices on the left and three on the right.
composition.receipt: Wide, compact, two-column paper brief rather than a long vertical strip.
composition.opening_view: Show the complete printed receipt within a typical desktop opening viewport wherever practical.
composition.mobile: Move service choices into two compact columns above the printer. Keep the paper readable and avoid horizontal overflow.

physical_details: Decorative barcode without fabricated transaction data

receipt_layout.header: ITCS logo and Your business. Our expertise.
receipt_layout.metadata: SERVICE BRIEF and ITCS service reference
receipt_layout.content_rule: This is a service brief, not a priced quotation. Do not invent discounts, prices, guarantees or deadlines.

animation.initial_load: The first receipt slowly feeds out of the slot when the page opens.
animation.selection: Selecting a service feeds out its receipt.
animation.motion: Translate the paper from behind a clipped slot into its final position, with gentle feed pauses.
animation.important: Animate the physical paper, not a slow fade or staggered reveal of each line of service text.
animation.rapid_selection: Cancel the previous feed and render the latest selected service correctly.
animation.manual_replay: Provide a small Print again control.
animation.status: Announce printing and completion with a polite live region.

alison.name: Alison
alison.heading: Meet Alison. More gets done.
alison.subheading: Support. Sales. Everyday operations. One connected part of your team.
alison.description: Handle routine enquiries, follow-ups and information gathering—even beyond office hours. Connect Alison to your business tools, with clear handovers when a person is needed.
claims_to_avoid: Alison can replace every human role.
Alison independently makes regulated compliance decisions.
The prototype is already connected to live business systems.

character.direction: Professional adult female business character with a restrained British presentation.
character.implementation: A genuine animated 3D character rather than a static photograph or cartoon.
avoid: Unnecessary visual separation from the ITCS page
character.licensing: Preserve the original licence and attribution files. Verify the actual asset licence before reuse.
character.fallback: Use the existing portrait only if the 3D renderer or model fails.

voice.delivery: Prerecorded local clips in the previous prototype.
rules: Audio starts only after explicit user interaction.
Provide a visible mute or voice toggle.
Stop speech when leaving the section, opening another dialog, changing page or hiding the browser tab.

interaction.business_name: Allow visitors to picture Alison in their business using an optional business-name field.
interaction.storage: Session storage only for the prototype business name.
interaction.scenario_selection: Four business contexts, each with three relevant examples.
interaction.conversation: Guided customer choices and approximately four Alison responses per scenario.
interaction.notes: Show what information was gathered, which systems could be involved and where a human handover would occur.
interaction.experience_language: Alison introduces herself as Alison. Do not repeatedly interrupt with 'I am a virtual assistant' or spoken demo disclaimers.
interaction.transparency: One discreet Interactive preview label is sufficient. Do not imply real calls or live account access.

examples.title: Track an order
examples.flow: Ask for an order reference, describe a hypothetical order lookup, explain tracking information and offer a useful next step.

examples.title: Handle a complaint
examples.flow: Listen to the issue, acknowledge the concern, gather details, explain the next action and prepare a clear handover.

examples.title: Start a return
examples.flow: Gather the order and return reason, explain a policy-based process and prepare a return request.

examples.title: Arrange a viewing
examples.flow: Understand the property interest, gather availability and contact information, and prepare a booking request.

examples.title: Request a valuation
examples.flow: Gather property details, location and preferred contact time for the agency team.

examples.title: Follow up an enquiry
examples.flow: Continue a property enquiry and give the agent a concise summary of the prospect's needs.

examples.title: Report an issue
examples.flow: Gather symptoms, affected users, urgency and attempted troubleshooting before routing the issue.

examples.title: Check a ticket
examples.flow: Gather a ticket reference and illustrate how a connected support system could provide an update.

examples.title: Prepare a new starter
examples.flow: Gather role, start date, equipment and access requirements, with approvals retained by the appropriate team.

examples.title: Qualify an enquiry
examples.flow: Understand requirements, timeline and contact details, then prepare a useful sales handover.

examples.title: Prepare a compliance review
examples.flow: Gather required information and organise a review pack for a qualified specialist.

examples.title: Prepare a recurring summary
examples.flow: Illustrate gathering routine updates and preparing a team summary.

sample_conversation.speaker: Alison
sample_conversation.text: Hello, I’m Alison. I can help you find out where your delivery is. Could you share your order reference, please? You’ll usually find it at the top of your confirmation email.

sample_conversation.speaker: Alison
sample_conversation.text: Thank you. Could you confirm the postcode used for the delivery?

sample_conversation.speaker: Alison
sample_conversation.text: Thank you. The tracking information shows your parcel is with the courier. I can explain the latest update and help you with the next step.

sample_conversation.speaker: Alison
sample_conversation.text: I can pass the order details and your concern to the support team, so you won’t need to explain everything again.

alison.cta: Make Alison part of your team.

sectors.heading: Support that fits the way you work.
sectors.description: A school, a practice and a growing office need different things from technology. Start with what matters in your world.

faq.question: Can we start with just one service?
faq.answer: Yes. You can start with a single issue, a project or ongoing support. We’ll discuss other services when they’re relevant to what you need.

faq.question: Can you work with our existing IT team?
faq.answer: We can discuss support alongside your team or a fully outsourced service. We agree who looks after what before work starts.

faq.question: Will switching disrupt our business?
faq.answer: We’ll review your existing services, contracts and dependencies with you, then agree a transition plan before making changes.

faq.question: What happens when we get in touch?
faq.answer: We talk about your business and what you need help with. From there, we identify the right people and agree a useful next step.

Dispose animation, audio and observer resources when components unmount.

asset_recovery.availability_warning: The user replaced the GitHub repository. Old URLs and local assets may no longer be available.
asset_recovery.rule: This JSON is a recreation specification, not an embedded backup of source code, models, audio or images. Inspect available files before promising exact asset recovery.
asset_recovery.if_character_assets_are_missing: Implement the Alison section structure and conversations, then obtain a suitable licensed animated character. Do not silently replace the requested interactive character with a stock photograph.
asset_recovery.if_voice_assets_are_missing: Keep readable conversations functional and provide voice only when suitable licensed clips or an authorised voice service are available.

requirements: No hover-only access to essential content
No essential information conveyed only by animation
accessibility_and_interaction.motion_policy: Use one memorable physical interaction at a time. Supporting sections should remain calm.

content_rules: Describe business outcomes before technical detail.
Do not fabricate statistics, ratings, response times or client results.
Do not display research dates, source-check notes or archive commentary.
Keep useful source records in internal documentation.
Do not label every interaction as a demo.
Do not hide actual limitations of form submission or live integrations.
Do not make Alison's compliance examples imply independent professional judgement.
Keep service details concise enough to understand quickly.
acceptance_criteria: ITCS exists as a dedicated section or route within the new portfolio repository.
The printer is the default homepage banner experiment.
The folder banner is preserved as a separate selectable alternative.
Only one banner is rendered at a time.
The desktop printer composition is wide and compact.
The first receipt visibly feeds out on arrival over approximately 2.6 seconds.
Service selection updates the receipt correctly, including rapid repeated selection.
Reduced-motion settings show the finished paper immediately.
All six ITCS service categories are represented.
Navigation reflects a future multi-page website.
Unfinished navigation destinations do not load inner pages.
The customer section contains no research-style source notes.
Alison covers support, sales, chat and routine business workflows.
Alison conversations remain usable without audio.
The design is responsive, keyboard accessible and free of horizontal overflow.
Forms do not falsely claim successful live submission.
Real assets retain their licences and attribution records.
execution_instruction_for_codex: Inspect the repository and its instructions first. Reuse recoverable ITCS assets and code where possible. Build the ITCS section using the repository's existing framework, implement both banner variants, preserve the full-site navigation structure without activating unfinished pages, and validate the actual desktop and mobile result with browser screenshots and interaction checks. Keep the user informed of missing assets or material limitations. Do not stop at a mockup or generic placeholder page.
